title: Introducing the topic of muscle dysmorphia (aka bigorexia)
summary: NH introduces muscle dysmorphia (bigorexia), a distorted perception of one's own size, as the most important health topic on his natural bodybuilding channel. He describes early reverse dysmorphia as a beginner, then still feeling small with 18-inch arms, and warns that taking PEDs to cure dysmorphia only makes it grow and endangers health. His main mission for the channel is to keep people natural.

claims.claim: Body dysmorphia is a mental illness where your perception of your own body is distorted; in bodybuilding it usually means seeing yourself much smaller (bigorexia), but can also mean seeing yourself fatter.
Muscle dysmorphia is something every lifter will face eventually; enhanced lifters are those who succumbed to it.
Beginners often experience reverse dysmorphia, seeing themselves as much bigger than they are.
At 17, after a few months of dumbbell training, he thought he was hugely muscular, but actually had 13-inch arms, a six-pack and weighed maybe 160 lbs.
Reverse dysmorphia quickly flips into the opposite: even with a good physique you look small in the mirror, in photos and looking down.
He has 18-inch arms as a natural, objectively high on the natural curve, yet still feels they are small.
Knowing you have dysmorphia doesn't make it easy to navigate, and there's no guarantee it ever goes away.
Constant exposure to bigger, stronger physiques on YouTube fitness worsens how lifters feel about themselves.
People suffering from dysmorphia eventually take PEDs thinking that getting big enough will cure it, but dysmorphia grows with you; at 19-inch arms he would still feel small.
Using PEDs to fix dysmorphia makes it worse because health is now at stake and it demands 'just a bit more' indefinitely, which can end in depression, self-harm or death from abuse.
His primary reason for the channel is to discourage people from taking PEDs and keep them natural; convincing one person makes it worthwhile.
Fitness and lifting should be healthy and make you feel better.
